author: Han Li,Lucy Quaggin
description:
On tote bags distributed by Asian-owned businesses in the US state of Georgia, three Asian-American women appeared in a design inspired by the Three Ladies rice brand. The bags were part of a campaign that put a voting twist on the online “Asian baby girl” meme.
“We had an ‘Asian Ballot Girls’ campaign,” said Chany Chea, programme director of the Asian-American Advocacy Fund. “We had merch which went viral.”
As Democrats won races in Republican strongholds across the southern United States in...
title: How Asian-American campaigners helped turn the US deep-red South blue

author: Holly Chik
description:
A leading cybersecurity scientist in the Chinese military, Guo Shize, has been removed from the website of the country’s top national research institute.
Guo, 57, a researcher at the Information Technology Security Research Centre of the People’s Liberation Army, was elected to the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) in 2023.
It is not known when his page was removed from the academy’s website, but Chinese media reports noted the change on Monday. Neither the academy nor Beijing’s defence ministry...
title: PLA cybersecurity scientist Guo Shize removed from Chinese Academy of Sciences website

author: Wang Qing
description:
On November 22, 2021, President Xi Jinping and the leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) jointly announced the establishment of a China-Asean Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, marking a new milestone in the history of this important relationship.
Guided by the vision of a closer community with a shared future and with sustained efforts to build a peaceful, secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable region as our common home, China and Asean have jointly nurtured one of...
title: China-Asean partnership is helping build common home and shared future

author: Igor Patrick
description:
China’s embassy in Santo Domingo accused the United States on Monday evening of “sinister intentions” and mocked Washington for “congratulating” the Dominican Republic on closing a Chinese-run cardboard factory.
The rebuke came hours after Juan Pablo Segura, who leads the US State Department’s Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs, praised Dominican authorities on social media for “taking decisive action to shut down a massive, illegal, Chinese-operated cardboard factory”.
Operating without...
title: China mocks US ‘congratulations’ over Dominican closure of Chinese-run factory

author: Alyssa Chen,Albee Zhang
description:
China hawks in Washington could weaponise allegations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence, despite denials from Beijing, Chinese experts warn.
They said controversy would give US hardliners fresh ammunition to push for tougher curbs on AI chip exports to China.
One of them compared the potential fallout to the 2023 “spy balloon” incident, when the US shot down in its airspace what Beijing said was an off-course weather balloon, putting relations on ice for...
title: Will Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair become another ‘spy balloon’ saga for US-China ties?

author: Carol Yang
description:
The presidents of the US and China are set to meet again at next week’s Apec summit, but observers expect few tangible bilateral deliverables to emerge from their talks.
The face-to-face meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping will be the third between the two leaders this year, following reciprocal state visits in May and September.
They are also expected to meet at the Group of 20 summit in the United States in December. In each case, global markets will be watching closely to see how...
title: Xi and Trump set for Apec talks, but major deliverables expected to wait for G20

author: Chao Kong
description:
Light travels through conventional optical fibres at about 200,000km per second – about two-thirds the speed it travels in a vacuum – because the signals are passing through solid glass.
When vast amounts of data are exchanged between computing centres hundreds or thousands of kilometres apart, this difference amounts to a substantial delay.
Now, Chinese researchers have unveiled optical fibre that replaces the solid glass core with air, cutting the data transmission delay by about 30 per cent...
title: Data link trial: Chinese team finds hollow-core fibre cuts lag 30% across 1,000km

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China has handed over the remains of American airmen who were killed during World War II while carrying supplies over the Himalayas.
The Chinese and US militaries held a handover ceremony in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan province, on Tuesday to transfer remains excavated from sites along “the Hump”, a treacherous airlift route between India and China.
The Chinese defence ministry did not disclose how many sets of remains were handed over or whether the servicemen’s identities had been...
title: China hands over remains of US airmen killed during World War II supply missions

author: William Zheng
description:
A Chinese state employee who falsely accused a colleague of spying for Beijing after losing out on a coveted overseas posting has been penalised by the Ministry of State Security.
The country’s top intelligence agency made the rare decision to shed light on the case using its social media account on Tuesday in a bid to highlight the consequences of making false accusations.
The perpetrator, identified only by his surname, Liu, earned a master’s degree from a prestigious university in 2018 and...
title: China warns against fake spy claims after jealous public servant frames rival

author: Alcott Wei
description:
China’s most senior general has called for joint efforts by military and civilian officials to combat corruption within the People’s Liberation Army, specifically targeting the development of major weapons systems.
General Zhang Shengmin, vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC) and a former PLA anti-corruption chief, made the remarks in a supplementary reader for the resolution adopted at the Communist Party’s latest plenum.
Published earlier this month, the collection features...
title: China’s top general targets PLA arms in call for joint military-civilian corruption watch

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
US Marines deployed across the western Pacific could struggle to sustain their forces, move missile batteries and secure permission to launch operations from allied territory in a conflict with China, according to assessments by Marine Corps officers and independent analysts.
Writing separately in the November issue of the US Naval Institute’s Proceedings journal, retired lieutenant general Stephen Sklenka and serving Lieutenant Colonel Merritt Mitchell identified vulnerabilities in the...
title: Could US Marines sustain a war with China? Officers warn of Pacific weaknesses

author: Nayan Seth,Dewey Sim,William Zheng
description:
Top US business leaders, including Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk and Mastercard’s Michael Miebach, are expected to join Donald Trump’s delegation to China for next week’s Apec summit, the South China Morning Post understands.
Nvidia chief Jensen Huang had been in talks to join, but his participation is now in doubt amid a controversy that has rocked his company and the wider tech industry.
Sources told the SCMP that Musk, Miebach and Huang were among the executives the US president planned to...
title: Elon Musk and Michael Miebach to join Trump at Apec in Shenzhen. What about Jensen Huang?

author: Zhang Tong
description:
United States President Donald Trump has recounted stories from air force pilots who told him they encountered UFOs, while saying he remains sceptical and has seen no evidence of an alleged secret programme to study unidentified flying objects.
“I’m not too much of a believer,” Trump said, while describing the pilots as credible people whose accounts he took seriously.
“They’ve told me things that are very strange. They said that, in certain cases, they said, ‘Yes, there’s something going on out...
title: Trump recounts pilots’ ‘very strange’ UFO stories but says he remains sceptical

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Firefighters used military drones, heavy transport aircraft and seaplanes in a large-scale drill in southwest China on Monday, as part of efforts to bring the latest technologies into emergency response operations.
The exercise involved more than 1,600 personnel and over 40 aircraft and simulated a major forest fire in a high-altitude mountainous region of Chongqing, state broadcaster CCTV reported.
Aircraft in the drill included the Wing Loong II and Twin-Tailed Scorpion – both unmanned aerial...
title: China uses military drones, heavy-lift and C909 planes in huge forest fire drill

author: Nayan Seth,Lucy Quaggin
description:
The fallout from the Nvidia scandal may test the fragile truce between the US and China, analysts say, as calls in Washington grow to tighten semiconductor export controls just days before US President Donald Trump is due to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China.
“I think that [scandal] could have a bigger impact down the line during the meeting in Miami or even further down the line,” said Ilaria Mazzocco, a senior fellow at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies....
title: Nvidia scandal may test fragile US-China truce, experts say
